interpretation: Temperature interacts with pigment genotype/pathway architecture, but its phenotypic or fitness sign is not universal across natural systems.
mechanistic_modifier_hypothesis: Tissue specificity and pathway position of pigment loss can reverse the fitness consequences of thermal stress: floral-specific regulatory suppression can permit white flowers while preserving extra-floral flavonoid functions, whereas systemic early-pathway nulls can make white genotypes heat-sensitive.
hard_nonclaims: four systems are mechanistic case studies, not an unbiased meta-analysis
no cross-system sign p-value is reported
does not establish temperature as the universal driver of FCP white/nonwhite geometry
